extracted.intended_audience: national governments, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders participating in OGP action plan processes
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for how OGP national members should design, co-create, implement, and monitor OGP action plans to ensure inclusive, transparent, accountable and ambitious public participation throughout the action plan cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information regarding OGP processes, activities, decisions and outcomes should be easily accessible by any interested stakeholder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively publish and disseminate information in the most relevant format and through the most appropriate means throughout the action plan cycle and provide regular progress updates on commitment development and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive participation (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow for a diversity of voices to meaningfully participate in the OGP process, identify priorities, and propose solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct outreach to minority or traditionally underrepresented groups and ensure access to information regarding the opportunities for participation and input; design processes so any interested stakeholders (citizens, civil society organizations, government departments, subnational governments, parliament, academics, private sector, etc.) can provide ideas and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear information about the results of consultation processes and the outcomes of commitment implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why certain stakeholder priorities were not included and the reasons for any changes or delays during commitment implementation; publish results and responses so stakeholders can hold actors to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and ambition (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to go beyond the minimum requirements and innovate on ways to develop, co-create and implement more ambitious and transformative open government reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use highly transparent, participatory and collaborative processes as an opportunity to encourage ambition; view minimum requirements as starting points rather than goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 1: Establish a space for ongoing dialogue and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a space (or platform) for ongoing dialogue and collaboration between government, civil society and other non-governmental stakeholders throughout the action plan cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition: platforms build trust, joint problem-solving, broaden constituency and are correlated with stronger commitments and completion rates. Approaches encouraged: establish a multi-stakeholder forum (MSF) or equivalent; ensure inclusivity and balanced representation so no constituency is over- or underrepresented; publish clear rules on selection, decision-making and external accountability; meet regularly (at least every 6 months); proactively communicate and report back on activities, decisions and results; ensure the platform has necessary mandate (e.g., decree, memorandum); coordinate government participation via a government point of contact in consultation with civil society; have civil society select its members through a fair transparent process led by civil society; create engagement paths for academia and private sector; provide remote participation options for at least some meetings; actively encourage participation of underrepresented groups and consider gender/diversity assessments to inform outreach. Minimum requirement (1.1): a space for ongoing dialogue with participation from both government and civil society and other non-governmental representatives that meets at least every six months is established, and its basic rules on participation are public. Assessment: IRM will develop assessment criteria once approved; for compliance IRM will look for evidence of action toward meeting minimum requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 2: Provide open, accessible and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide open, accessible and timely information about activities and progress within a member’s participation in OGP throughout the action plan cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition: follow the principle of maximum transparency; publish relevant information proactively in relevant formats and channels so the widest possible population can access and understand it; provide regular updates on commitment development and implementation. Approaches encouraged: maintain a public OGP website or web page (searchable); publish information on leading/participating agencies, contacts, processes, agendas, minutes and relevant documents; clearly identify lead agency and point of contact with public contact info; where possible publish information about civil society organizations participating in MSF; use non-technical language and online/offline tools; publish in all administrative languages and consider accessibility for visual/auditory impairment; publish regular updates (at least every six months) on progress toward milestones, delays and next steps; publish process and completion information in machine-readable open formats where relevant; provide a feature to allow public comment on progress updates. Minimum requirements: 2.1 maintain a public OGP website dedicated to the member's participation; 2.2 maintain a publicly available document repository on the OGP online site providing access to documents related to the OGP process (including evidence of co-creation and implementation) and update it regularly (at least twice a year). Assessment: IRM will develop assessment criteria once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 3: Provide inclusive and informed opportunities for public participation during development
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implement a co-creation process for the development of the action plan that allows interested stakeholders to provide ideas, feedback, identify priorities and propose commitments, with special outreach to underrepresented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition: high public participation is linked to more diverse and ambitious action plans. Approaches encouraged: develop a co-creation timeline outlining stages, roles and expectations; develop a methodology covering awareness-raising, participation of diverse actors, input gathering, processing, drafting proposals, approvals and decision-making; use a combination of open in-person meetings and online engagement adapted to context to enable remote participation; conduct outreach activities to raise awareness and recruit liaison contacts for underrepresented communities; publish in advance the timeline, methodology and decision-making process and provide appropriate notice of events and draft commitments; share agendas and reading materials at least one calendar week before meetings where commitments or drafts will be discussed or decided; use appropriate participation methods (thematic working tables, written feedback, online discussions, surveys, remote/in-person meetings) and schedule meetings at times/locations that maximize participation. Minimum requirements: 3.1 publish the co-creation timeline and overview of opportunities for stakeholders at least two weeks before the start of action plan development; 3.2 conduct outreach activities to raise awareness and opportunities to get involved; 3.3 develop a mechanism to gather inputs from a range of stakeholders during an appropriate period for the chosen mechanism. Assessment: IRM will develop assessment criteria once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 4: Provide reasoned responses and ensure ongoing dialogue during co-creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reasoned responses to stakeholder input and ensure ongoing dialogue between government and non-government stakeholders during action plan development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition: reasoned responses are highly correlated with ambition, completion and early results; ongoing dialogue (iterative communication, refinement and feedback) increases buy-in and implementation likelihood. Approaches encouraged: facilitate mechanisms for direct communication to respond to process questions; publish and disseminate all written contributions and responses to action plan development; publish a summary of stakeholder contributions (regardless of acceptance); assess commitment proposals through an open and transparent process and publish an overview of responses to proposals; once commitments are drafted, present reasoning for selection and justifications for proposals not adopted; provide a range of options for stakeholder feedback on draft commitments (written, online, surveys, meetings) open for an adequate duration (at least 2 weeks); if process separates commenting from input-gathering, each phase should be at least two weeks. Minimum requirement: 4.1 document and report back or publish written feedback to stakeholders on how their contributions were considered during development of the action plan. Assessment: IRM will develop assessment criteria once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard 5: Provide inclusive opportunities for ongoing dialogue during implementation and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure continued stakeholder dialogue and participation during implementation and monitoring of the action plan to support completion and stronger results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition: continued engagement during implementation correlates with higher completion and stronger results; can include additional commenting opportunities, peer exchanges, ministerial engagement and challenge commitments; co-ownership of implementation by civil society via thematic working tables is possible. Approaches encouraged: hold open meetings or maintain channels for implementing agencies to provide updates and respond to stakeholder input; monitor and deliberate on improvements to implementation; maintain a public dashboard with up-to-date information on implementation progress, delays and corroborating evidence to complement the document repository; prepare a self-assessment report once a year based on repository/dashboard information and hold at least a two-week public consultation to gather comments on the report; include inclusive analysis tools (e.g., gender/diversity analysis) to identify implementation gaps; publish self-assessment reports and all written comments on the OGP website/webpage. Minimum requirement: 5.1 hold at least two meetings every year with civil society to present results on implementation and collect comments. Assessment: IRM will develop assessment criteria once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan length (rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules related to action plan duration and refresh cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries can choose a two-year or four-year action plan. Four-year plans must include a mandatory refresh at the two-year mark consisting of a shortened co-creation process for updating or modifying commitments. The minimum requirements for the refresh period are 3.1 (publish co-creation timeline and opportunities two weeks before development) and 4.1 (document and report back on how contributions were considered) and will be assessed by the IRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery windows and timeliness (rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when action plan implementation cycles start and permissible delivery windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries select from two implementation cycles that formally start either June 30 or December 31 and end on the same date two or four years later. Action plans can be delivered starting six months before and up to two months after the selected start date; afterwards the country must use the next delivery window. A country is considered to have acted contrary to OGP process if it fails to deliver an action plan within one year after completion of its previous action plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment approach by the Independent Reporting Mechanism (IRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRM will determine criteria and assess compliance with minimum requirements for each Standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For compliance purposes, the IRM will determine if there is evidence of action toward meeting the minimum requirements in each case. Several Standards note that the IRM will develop the detailed assessment sections after approval by the OGP Chair & Steering (C&S). Where the Standards specify minimum requirements (e.g., 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 5.1), the IRM's assessment will look for documented evidence that these have been met (e.g., public websites, published timelines, meeting records, published feedback, document repositories, meeting frequency).
